You see my playtime. I'm playing this game for too long, so if I say I don't like it, I'd lie.
The game is good on the bigger picture, I like it a lot and there is yet nothing like this game on the market.
The actual problems are that Gaijin is gradually making its player base unable to play the vehicles of the highest ranks due to not having enough money to buy them and repair them after they've been destroyed, thus forcing them to either buy premium or leave the high ranks.
I am playing this game for long enough to afford to play on high ranks and even I notice that, without premium time or vehicles, most of the time I'll lose currency.
This is a dishonest tactic to make the player base spend money in this game and being a free-to-play game doesn't justify their methods. There are other successful free-to-play games that don't have a broken economic system to force its player base to switch to premium rewards. I believe Gaijin can do the same if they would care enough.
In conclusion, I can not recommend this game to any beginner at this moment. Not until Gaijin makes a viable economic system even for non-premium users.

War Thunder is the only game where I log in thinking I’m a skilled pilot and log off 30 minutes later questioning my entire existence, my eyesight, and whether my keyboard secretly works for the enemy team.

You don’t play War Thunder. War Thunder plays you.
One second you’re majestically climbing at 4,000 meters like a World War II ace, the next second some guy named “xX_RealPilot1944_Xx” deletes you from the sky before you even finish saying, “Where did that come fro—”

The learning curve isn’t a curve.
It’s a vertical takeoff.

The realism is incredible. My plane stalls realistically. My tank explodes realistically. My sanity deteriorates realistically.

You start the game thinking:
“I’ll just try one match.”

Four hours later:
“I now know the armor thickness of a 1943 Panzer better than my own Social Security number.”

The community is a beautiful mix of:
• History professors
• Flight engineers
• Absolute maniacs who can identify your tank by the sound of your engine from 2 kilometers away

And the grind?
Oh, the grind is spiritual.
You don’t unlock vehicles. You earn them through suffering.

Recommend this game to anyone who wishes to suffer.

This game is VERY qualitative, you can tell that the developers took their time when developing each vehicle in the game. It is a must try. However, the business model of this game is disgusting, it takes a VERY long time to research vehicles once you get to rank 3 and above.

I especially hate how they keep on advertising the modern vehicles as if the game allowed you to use them from the start or at least close to start, but no, it takes months to get to that point.

Over all the game is pretty fun, I can recommend it. However, it is an extremely grindy game.

Phlydaily, one of the biggest content creators for this game, coined the phrase "War Thunder: It's almost fun". That phrase alone is better at describing the game than any review could ever be.

War Thunder has amazing controls, fantastic visuals, has incredible physics, something like 1500 vehicles, 30 maps per mode, gets consistent updates and events and yet still fails in that one crucial aspect, it's barely fun to actually play.

Because the game is the only one of its kind with no real competition, you keep playing it hoping it will get better at some point because it's all you got, but it never does get better. The game only gets more and more frustrating and develops into the same sort of harmful addiction you'd find in gambling addicts or alcoholics and it took hundreds of hours to realise and break that addiction. Just remember that early on the game is nice to you. If you ever think: "it's not that bad", thats just because the game is still in the process of getting you hooked. Stay away is my advice.
